scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: Hi IT!! The upstairs design floor (the 172.16.30.x
machines) has STOPPED EXISTING for us downstairs -- from my PC5 (172.16.10.x)
every one of them times out, while my own floor is totally fine!! The big
switch that joins the floors has obviously lost its marbles -- I'm told it
keeps the floors on separate "lanes", and clearly the ramp between our lane
and theirs has collapsed!! Please fix the big switch, rebuild the ramp
between the floors, and reconnect me to design -- deadlines!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce an outage between the 172.16.10.0/24 (“downstairs”) and 172.16.30.0/24 (“design”) networks. Inter-VLAN reachability is currently healthy. From the reported source (pc5 = 172.16.10.5) I directly tested to multiple design hosts and observed clean connectivity: pc5 → pc12/pc13/pc14 all returned 0% packet loss with ~0.9–1.9 ms RTT. The topology-wide probe also shows normal cross-LAN reachability (e.g., 172.16.30.x → 172.16.10.8 succeeding with low RTT and no loss). This confirms that the routing “ramp” between the VLANs and the upstream aggregation (mswitch0 and its trunks) are functioning.

Mechanistically, if the “big switch” or a trunk carrying VLANs toward the router had failed, we would see consistent bidirectional loss between the subnets, not clean, low-latency replies. Likewise, if the inter-VLAN router or default gateways were down, all 10.x↔30.x tests would fail, which they do not.

Localization: No abnormal behavior observed on pc5, design hosts, or the interconnecting switches/routers at this time. The upstream aggregation path (mswitch0 and linked access switches) is passing traffic normally.

Root cause: Not reproducible; the earlier symptom was transient or host-specific, not a current network device fault.

Corrective fix: No changes required. If the issue recurs, capture on-the-spot evidence from pc5 (arp -n, ip route, ping/traceroute to 172.16.30.x and the default gateway) and note exact timestamps to correlate with switch/router logs for any fleeting trunk or ARP anomalies.
